utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Moore: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Witness, can we just deal please with the end of your evidence last night. You'd said that you'd been in, I believe, the X-ray room, that you had been separated, male and female, and that you had gone on a bus, and mentioned two individuals that you remembered. I would like, however, to return to the evening of the 19th when you arrived at the Vukovar Hospital that day with your wife. Now, can we deal with the evening of the 19th? When you arrived at the Vukovar Hospital, did you see any persons in uniform there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may correct you. I arrived in the hospital on the 19th in the morning. Once I arrived there, I didn't see any JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw JNA soldiers on the -- at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw JNA soldiers in the hospital was on the 19th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's difficult to assess time. You say evening. Are you able to say whether it's early evening or late evening? Can you give us some indication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening at around 9.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was in the X-ray room of the Vukovar Hospital, the radiology department. Mr. Kuzmic entered the room where we were together with soldiers. He was accompanied by two soldiers. His name was Bogdan Kuzmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him for many years because he used to work as the receptionist or doorman at the Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what way was he dressed that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogdan Kuzmic wore the old JNA uniform, a plain winter JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers were looking for Mr. Milicko Vukovic, and through him they wanted to find Mr. -- a gentleman who used to work in Nama, a department store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm thinking about it right now, but it keeps escaping me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In any event, did they find Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They found Mr. Vukovic, and they left the room, the X-ray room, and took him somewhere else. Mr. Vukovic came back to the room where we were some 15 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other person whose name you cannot remember, are you able to say whether they found that person or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't find person, because they received information that at that particular time that person was not in the hospital. If I may add, I just remembered his name. That gentleman's name is Zeljko Batarelo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was Bogdan Kuzmic and the two soldiers, how long were they in the hospital that you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them only while they were in the X-ray room, not later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The uniform that Bogdan Kuzmic was wearing, did it have any rank as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it well, but he said that he had a rank of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the X-ray room that evening, the evening of the 19th and perhaps morning of the 20th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of November, 1991, I stayed there the entire night until the morning. I mean, the X-ray room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give the Court an indication of when it was when you left the X-ray room on the 20th, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left the X-ray room in the morning on the 20th of November, 1991, between 7.30 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reason for you leaving the X-ray room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told, all of us who were present, to go and assemble in the hospital yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go and assemble in the hospital yard as requested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us went out together with their family members. As we were leaving the basement area of the Vukovar Hospital where the radiology department is, we had to go through the entrance which is opposite from the main entrance. There were soldiers awaiting us there who separated men to one side and women and children to another side. We were lined up there at that entrance to the hospital; that is to say, we were lined up opposite from the main entrance of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you were separated. Did that apply to your wife and yourself? Where you both separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the line that you went into, was it only men or women? Can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Solely men as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate in general terms how many men were in that queue or -- well, queue perhaps is the best way of describing it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be hard for me to estimate a final number or even an approximate number. At any rate, all of the men who were in the hospital at that time. This is the entrance going towards Gunduliceva Street, and we were lined up one next to each other all the way up to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will show you a diagram in a minute, but before we do that, when you were about to go into the line or at the line, did the JNA soldiers or any other parties do anything do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers were given orders to search us, those of us who were lined up there. First they verbally demanded that we surrender all sharp objects, items, anything that could be used to hurt somebody; that is to say, knives, weapons, or any other sharp items. Following that, they searched our hand-luggage. All of us had some bags with us carrying our personal belongings, and the soldiers searched these bags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person or the soldier who searched you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took out everything out of my bag. I mostly had clothes. However, my socks remained at the bottom of the bag. I had five pairs of male socks, and they were rolled up in a ball. He saw that there was something in the bag and he stepped on it. I asked him not to step on my bag, telling him that I would take out all of its contents. He got offended. He moved a step away from me. He cursed me using an offensive word and then said, "All of you would be two metres below the ground if it weren't for a large number of our people captured by your people." Later on, as we were travelling from the barracks to Sremska Mitrovica, I noticed that this same soldier was accompanying us, and in the conversation that he had with the other soldier, I learned that his name was Pero. That's how this other soldier addressed him. I also learned that he hailed from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the line, can you remember the names of people whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only person whose name I know is Mr. Emil Cakalic, and Mr. Tomislav Pap. These two persons. There were other familiar persons there but I don't know their first and last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the hospital courtyard, were you able to assess who was in charge apparently of the JNA soldiers and operation at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, a major of the JNA was in charge of the entire operation. Everything transpired under his control and on his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you subsequently find out the name of that officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know the name of that officer. However, later on when I came to the holding centre in Sremska Mitrovica, from other soldiers I learned that that major's name was Veselin Sljivancanin. I don't know how other people learned his name. When I left the camp and arrived back in Zagreb in Croatia, then on a TV report -- in a TV report I saw that same major and recognised him as the JNA major, Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe to the Court his attitude or air at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That major issued orders to his soldiers. He was moving about around the hospital, and he seemed to be a very arrogant officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He seemed insolent and arrogant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other officer in JNA uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't see any other JNA officers. However, later on from the prisoners who were with me at the camp, I learned that there was another officer in the hospital compound. He was a lieutenant, and that he was involved in the search conducted by the soldiers and also escorted people to the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now, please, to show you a document. It is page number 320191. It is known as, I hope, Annex A. Witness 31, have you got the document Annex A showing on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that you have seen before. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document I believe you helped create in 1995 with Mr. Djuro. 1996. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just deal, please, with it in a general way. You're in the fortunate position of having an electronic pen which I've tried to help you in working out. Would you be kind enough with that electronic pen to show us where the actual main hospital building is located on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main entrance is to my right as I'm seeing this on the screen. It is shown by the broken line in front of the hospital building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, please, to put your electronic pen on the screen, and we then have hopefully a red mark to show what you're talking about. So can you put a red mark, an X, showing where the main hospital building is on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we just mark that also with an A. Could you put a capital A and circle it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. Where exactly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can put the A wherever you wish, just so long as it's beside the X and we know to what it refers. So perhaps if you put the X and then the A above with a circle. And then a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, can you show us where the line of people was or men were prior to being bused away. Are you able to do that by drawing the red line around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There seems to be a line right round the square building. To what does that relate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line shows the path and the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Path and road of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an asphalt road -- or, rather, asphalt path more similar to a pedestrian path than one used by vehicles. However, opposite from the main entrance was the emergency room, and ambulances would normally go to that building and then travel back going around the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the diagram itself, at the very bottom we have in English, I presume, the word "buses." Can you see that? At 6.00, as is sometimes described. The very bottom of the drawing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what do those buses relate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came out of the hospital building and as we were lined up facing Gunduliceva Street, I saw that there were five buses parked in Gunduliceva Street, and this depicts these buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to assist us, can you just draw a line where the Danube River would be in relation to this diagram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Opposite from Gunduliceva Street is Ivo Lola Ribar Street, which is a one-way street travelling from the east to the west. Then behind that road is a block of private houses, and then immediately behind them is the Danube. So Gunduliceva Street we can say is opposite from the Danube River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just put a wiggly line, please, to show you where the Danube is? Can you use your magic pen to put it on the electronic score-board, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then finally, with B can you show us where it was that you went onto the buses? So if you do an X and a B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Where I came out or the buses, which do you mean? When I got onto the bus or this continuation of the straight line with two perpendicular lines, because that's where you reach the -- where you leave the hospital yard and reach Gunduliceva Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just put your pen on the score-board and mark for us the route that you took, please, before getting onto the buses. So can you do that and we'll be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be kind enough, as I say, to put a B and a cross where it was you got on the buses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then for completeness sake, in which direction did you then head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buses were right there facing west, facing the direction of Zagreb, generally speaking. Once all the detainees had been put on the buses, the buses backed about 20 or 30 metres into another road next to the hospital. They backed onto that road and drove down Bozidara Adzija Street in the direction of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, please, just put your pen on the screen and mark out the route that you took, and there we will leave it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender that amended document as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit 142.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say what happened to the wounded people from the hospital that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those found there, the wounded, the ill and the civilians who were in the building of the Vukovar Hospital were taken to the buses that were lined up there. Based on my information, the wounded were the first to be taken away and put on the first three buses. The civilians were the next to be taken away and then the sick people and the remaining staff, and we were put on the last two buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- are you able to remember any of the names of wounded people who were put onto those buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All I remember is the name of a civilian I knew. He was standing outside next to my bus, standing between the road and the pedestrian path to the hospital. He was lying there on a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of that person, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Martin Dosen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I deal with Martin Dosen, please. Who was Martin Dosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to know Martin Dosen as a boxer, a pugilist, from the Borovo boxing club. We go back a long way. He had some assignment or other in the Croatian army. He had been wounded somewhere or other, I'm not sure, and that was how he had ended up in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Martin Dosen that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, his daughter was standing next to his stretcher. Her name was Tanja, Tanja Dosen. She was standing next to him, but he was not brought onto any of our buses, and I have no idea how he eventually reached the place where he came to grief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When say "came to grief," firstly, where did he come to grief as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to grief at Ovcara. His body was later identified along with all the other people who were executed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Martin Dosen, you said, I believe, that he was lying on a stretcher. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say if he was receiving any medical treatment at that time or medical care?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I had seen him several days earlier, probably also on the 19th when I reached the hospital. It was on the hospital ground floor. He was lying on one of the hospital beds, or perhaps it was a stretcher. It was between urology and the orthopaedic ward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm really referring to you that when you actually see him on a stretcher beside the buses on the 20th, was he receiving any medical care at that time? If you can't remember, just say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. There were no medical staff there to assist him. Only his daughter was there, and she was not a medical worker. She was standing next to him, but she was the only one there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to deal with the actual bus that you got onto. How many people were actually on the bus approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus was full. All the seats were filled. Based on my experience of riding on a bus, a bus would normally have between 45 and 50 seats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of people who were on the same bus as you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the back of the bus, the last two rows of seats. There's a door there. Mr. Emil Cakalic was sitting next to me, and in front of us there was Djuro Knezic, Stjepan Sarik. On the same bus I saw Mr. Zlatko Jurisic, and some other people I knew whose names escape me right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were on the bus were any checks done to see either the numbers or the personnel who were inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a chance to see anyone counting people or checking anything. There was the driver plus two JNA soldiers, but they did not interfere with the far end of the bus. If I may just add something. It is just now that I have remembered having seen Tihomir Perkovic on that same bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone get off that bus before it left the hospital area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a call being shouted. I just heard this. Just outside the bus I saw Mr. Sljivancanin. I thought the order had been from him, but the people who had been called out to get off the bus told me that this was not in fact the case but that, rather, this had been ordered by the person who was in charge of the buses. He came in through the front door, and he asked us if there was anyone on that bus with a hospital ID allowing them to go to the hospital and to leave the hospital. Once this question had been asked, five persons left the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, were you holding a hospital identification card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just something for the transcript. We don't see the word "lieutenant" on the transcript. That's lines 9 to 13. I see that the word is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want to pin that down, Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No. I agree entirely that it was lieutenant that was said and that Sljivancanin was outside. Certainly that is the way I've understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The lieutenant associated with Mr. Sljivancanin or the man in charge of the buses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I will certainly clarify, if I may, in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you have mentioned the gentleman or the officer who came onto the bus, you have used the word, I believe, "lieutenant." Who was that lieutenant? Had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the man was, and there was no way I could see him. He was standing at the front door of the bus, but this was the officer who was in charge of the line-up, the search, and the physical process of actually taking the detainees to the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just try and clarify the situation so there is absolutely no misunderstanding? You have told us that you have found major -- as you then found out to be Major Sljivancanin and a lieutenant at the hospital earlier on, and here you're referring to a lieutenant on the bus. What everyone would like to know is if the lieutenant that you saw on the bus was the same lieutenant that you had sign in the hospital. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same one. Thank you. I think I asked you whether you had a hospital identification card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did confirm that. I left the bus afterwards. I got off the bus, and I addressed Major Veselin Sljivancanin. I didn't know his name at the time. I just knew that he was a JNA major. He had looked at the IDs of those other five detainees. He said their passes or IDs were all right, and he said they should go back to the hospital. He looked at my ID, but I seemed to have lost the photograph that was attached to it. So I produced my regular ID. I told the major that I was that same person and that he can check -- he could check with the other people if he so wished. He carefully looked at the ID. He returned it to me and he told me to go back onto the bus, which is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got back onto the bus, were there any other persons on the bus apart from the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Apart from two soldiers and the driver in the front part of the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two soldiers at the front of the bus, how do you know that they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed that that when the buses reached the JNA barracks in Vukovar. It was when that I saw this lieutenant get off the bus and order the soldiers that they weren't to release anyone or allow anyone to go in or out. The soldiers rose somewhat from their seats and this was when I was able to see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to deal with those soldiers for a moment. Were the soldiers armed at that time when you were on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the sort of weapons that they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to -- or were you able to assess of what unit they belonged to or the nature of their military attachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to see any of their insignia from close up to be able to tell which unit they belonged to, but I heard from the other victims on the bus that those were military policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you wait outside the hospital before you left on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite long, actually. Between one and two hours, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where you were going to at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone give any order for the buses to move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An order came for the buses to drive on to the barracks. This order had been issued by Major Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you could see, did the buses leave together or individually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I asked the question and deserved the answer. But when you say "one by one," did they move in convoy or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in convoy, one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know that you came from Vukovar or lived in Vukovar at that time. Had you been to the JNA barracks before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe in very general terms which part of the barracks that you were driven to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA barracks is on a street known as Sajmiste. This is when you leave Vukovar and head for the village of Negoslavci. To the left of the road is the JNA barracks. We -- it was towards the last stretch of the road near Negoslavci that we were taken. There were no residential buildings there. There was some sort of a yard with some sort of a porch to leave vehicles there, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you know at that time a place called Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away were you from the buildings at Velepromet when you parked the bus -- or the bus parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimate, the distance wasn't too great. 500 metres at most. That's before reaching Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the barracks, are you able to see or were you able to see if they were guarded by any persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see that. We took that entrance, a gate, and we were approaching those buildings that were inside the barracks compound. I did not actually see if it was guarded or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the bus stopped, did you see any other persons outside the bus or buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not when the bus stopped, but they arrived shortly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the buses entered the barracks compound and stopped, a group of men started running in our direction from the road down which we had arrived. I concluded that these people were Serb paramilitaries behaving in an extremely aggressive way, acting dangerous. They approached the bus with wooden poles and sticks which they used to bang on the bus. They were trying to look inside to see if they could recognise any of us. They were quite curious, I should say, and exceptionally aggressive. To the right of the bus, the bus that was parked there and the building there, I'm not sure if it was a garage or whatever its use happened to be, a group of soldiers arrived or, rather, persons wearing JNA uniforms, winter-time uniforms. These were no regular soldiers or conscripts. These people were slightly older.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to deal then, please, with that account in more detail. You or the interpreters have used the word "group." Are you able to give the Court an estimate of numbers who approach the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aggressive ones who approached, the paramilitaries, there might have been between 15 and 20 of them. As for those others who were difficult to identify, I wasn't sure if they were from the Vukovar TO or reservists of the JNA. There may have been between ten and a dozen of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to the conclusion that a group were -- they were paramilitaries? How did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, firstly -- firstly, as I say, those soldiers, in as far as they were soldiers at all, were in a drunken state, inebriated. They were dressed in a quite slovenly way, and their uniforms were quite disorderly. Some of them wore white bands or shoulder-straps around their shoulders, and some wore some sort of a sign that said "SAO Krajina Police force."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise any of the persons in that group? When I say "recognise," I don't mean that you knew their name but that you had seen them before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, then, I think, about the other group that came, somewhere between 10 and 12. Can you be now -- would you be kind enough to tell us how you came to the conclusion that -- I think that they were TOs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know what the actual difference was, but there were such military formations in Vukovar. These people wore winter JNA uniforms. And as I have already said to you, they were somewhat older than typical conscripts serving their military service in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say if any of them came from the Vukovar area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able or do you know any of their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. I knew well the persons there from previous times, and I was able to recognise them there. I will list their names. Milan Bulic, Jezdimir Stankovic, Radivoje Jakovljevic, Sreto Nedeljkovic, and Ilinka Stankovic. We called her Inka, but I'm not sure what her formal first name is. Veselinka. That's her first name. Veselinka Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were they behaving at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They acted normally. They were only interested in determining which prisoners on the bus they knew. They even talked to some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us about the windows or the buses being beaten with various wooden implements, and you suggested about trying to get you to turn round. Can you tell the Court, please, how that occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, as to whether they wanted to turn the bus upside down or not, I'm not sure, but they banged on the windows of the bus with these poles and sticks. They insulted us, cursed us. They threatened us, demanding that we turn around to face them so that they could perhaps recognise us. They called us Ustashas and murderers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether you use the word "threatened us," can you give, please, a general indication of the sort of threats that were being uttered against you so the Court can understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cursed us. They cursed our descendants. They cursed our families, insulted them with various curses. They cursed our mothers, fathers, children. They also banged on the bus with the sticks, and we took that to be a sufficient threat. They were quite aggressive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A threat of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They threatened us with wooden sticks, poles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever suggest what they would do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. As an order was issued to the soldiers that nobody was allowed in or out of the bus, they probably were unable to board the bus. They didn't try to do it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You use the phrase "exceptionally aggressive." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is clear what an aggressive person is. Somebody who threatens other people, threatens to beat them, curses them, and so on. Somebody who is prepared at any time to harm somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this was occurring, how long did this last? Are you able to assess?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that specifically. However, we sat on the buses for quite a long time in the barracks. In addition to the five buses which arrived from the hospital to the barracks, the sixth bus arrived later on as well. It was some 30 metres away from our buses. It arrived about half an hour later. The same group of people, upon seeing the sixth bus, left our buses and directed themselves to the sixth bus. When they abandoned sixth bus, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, here you were in the JNA barracks. Did at any time you see any officer or soldier interfere and stop this attack upon your bus or buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour might remember that this witness has a particular condition. I wonder if it might be an appropriate moment to adjourn for a short period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Moore, we might have the first break now and resume at a quarter to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just deal with two other matters administratively? Perhaps I should deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The first was yesterday when I went through the statements and gave the page number, I referred to 0131. It's -- the page numbers are rather opaque sometimes, and it really should be 0181 I think for statement 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the second matter is there is a personal difficulty that Your Honour is aware of for me on Friday. Unfortunately, that will also have to take up Monday, and I wonder if I could make an application, I know I've mentioned it to my learned friends who are privy to the content of my application, whether I could ask the Court's indulgence not to sit on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. That means we will not sit on Friday of this week or Monday of next week. Thank you, Mr. Moore. We will now adjourn and resume -- oh, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No thank you, Your Honour. I thought that we were ready for our break. I thought we've adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're training for the Olympics or something, Mr. Vasic. Very well. A quarter to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 31, you have -- it's been interpreted as sticks or poles, the word, I think, "palica." Do you know the word "palica"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that it can mean many things. Can you tell us the size of the sticks or poles that the people had outside the bus? Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was some that were shorter and some that were longer, going from 60 centimetres in length to one metre and 10 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you see anyone leaving the buses while you were at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers who probably had their instructions were looking for certain persons on buses. From my bus, they called out Mihajlo Kolesar and Mr. Bartol. I am not sure whether this is his first name or his last name. We used to call him Bartola. The two of them went the bus [as interpreted] and didn't return ever again. They left accompanied by soldiers in the direction of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it's right to say, is it, that you were aware that Kolesar and Bartola were taken back to the hospital. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I learned that once I arrived in Zagreb from Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember if the soldiers were looking for individuals whom you never saw again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that. The people that they were looking for, I think that all of them survived, at least the ones who were in that transport. If I may add, Mr. Kolesar is not alive any longer. He died of natural causes some four or five years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when you left the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left the JNA barracks in Vukovar at around 1430.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Obviously time is difficult to estimate. Why do you give that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a watch on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the JNA barracks, did you know where you were going to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the buses next stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time the buses stopped after that was in Vupik, which is a farm near Vukovar, and they stopped in front of a hangar which was used as a warehouse for agricultural machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got there, how many buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five buses arrived. The five that left the barracks arrived in Ovcara in front of that hangar one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look, please, at a diagram called Annex B. The page number is 00320193.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could that be shown to the witness on the electronic display unit, please. Now, before we refer to this document, I would like to play a very short video clip. It's -- the 65 ter number is 326. Has everybody got the -- can we play it now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: To assist the Court, this is a short video approaching the hangar on the right-hand side. I'd like to make that exhibit if I may, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it going to be identified as to date, et cetera, at any time, Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It will be identified. The process that I was hoping to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As long as you have that in mind, no need to explain it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is obviously done much later on. It's to assist everyone, so exactly they have locations and distances. Yes, it will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 143, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now can we return to Annex B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, it's just that I would like to ask the Prosecutor not to tell us what is on which side on the approach to what. I would prefer it if he left it to witnesses to comment on that. It's true that all of us in the courtroom know what is where, but still. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, unless the barracks becomes a tree, we may be in some difficulty. It's to assist all parties and the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you be kind enough, please, to look at Annex B, the diagram. Have you got it there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then adopt the same procedure, please, that we adopted with Annex A? Now, this document you have seen before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was compiled on the same day as Annex B; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just mark, as far as you remember, where it was the buses stopped.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow indicates the road leading from Vukovar to the farm in front of the hangar. The direction of the arrows indicates the direction from which the buses arrived towards this short concrete road which connects the road to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just then look, please, at what appears to be, and this is the only way I can do it, a path running towards the hangar. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark out for us, please, just with a small X where the path is. Please put your pen on the screen and mark it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the road, I mean the main road or you mean this driveway which connects the main road and the hangar?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark out the driveway.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, then, please, what this diagram represents? And do this slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch shows the main road and the driveway between the main road and the hangar. We can also see the contours of the hangar. It is not on scale. It doesn't show the actual dimensions of the hangar. And then the drawings inside the hangar depict the location where the prisoners were. These lines on each side of the driveway depict a group of paramilitaries who stood on both sides of the driveway creating a gauntlet through which all of the prisoners had to run and were beaten as they ran through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can we deal with the markings where you say you had to run the gauntlet. Can you please mark in red with your electronic pen where say the gauntlet was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the electronic pen or in some other way?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, always with the electronic pen, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but what kind of a mark do you want me to put?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just put an X where you say the gauntlet was, where the soldiers were located. It doesn't have to be an X or it can be a line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what does that mark show us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This mark depicts both sides of the driveway, the left side and the right side of the driveway, where the paramilitaries were who beat the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark, please, with a line where the paramilitaries were who beat the prisoners? Can you do a bold red line, please, or lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the outside or on the inside? Where do you want me to place it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us where the gauntlet was, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here on the driveway, on both sides of it, going all the way up to the entrance of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but what I want you to do, please, is to mark with your pen, to actually mark with your pen, where the paramilitary soldiers were who were beating prisoners as they were arriving.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Want kind of a mark do you want me to place?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A bold mark, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I deal, please, with the people who were located at this particular place? Firstly, who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people shown here with these lines are the people who had been brought in from the Vukovar Hospital and the barracks in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were they? Are you able to assist the Court about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were wounded persons there, the ill persons, civilians who used to work in the hospital, and some medical staff or, rather, some hospital staff in charge of the hospital security. They were Croatian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was happening to them as they arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses arrived one by one from the direction of Vukovar, and as they arrived, they stopped in front of the driveway, and then the prisoners went out through the front door. In front of the driveway, there were two or three soldiers standing there. Later, they made -- created this gauntlet. But initially as the prisoners came out of the buses, they robbed them of all of their belongings, took away their bags, gold and jewellery, necklaces, rings, and any other kind of other valuables that prisoners had on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you've used the word "gauntlet" on several occasions. What do you mean by that? Can you please not look at the diagram anymore and just focus on the question. What do you mean by the word "gauntlet"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers, some of them I'd seen in the barracks, and they arrived in Ovcara prior to us. They probably knew that the prisoners would be coming out of the buses and then would be taken to the hangar, so they lined themselves up in front of it in order to do what I have already described to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to describe again, please, what happened when the prisoners arrived off the bus.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoners were getting off the buses one by one. First, they were stopped by those two or three soldiers who robbed them. After that, they would proceed towards the hangar, passing the gauntlet on the way there, and they were beaten as they walked along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who beat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paramilitary soldiers. Serb paramilitaries. Those were no regular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how severely were they beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on who was where exactly and the angle that people were being beaten. They used wooden poles, and they used crutches, too, to hit people. It depends on who came from where and the exact timing of a person passing this gauntlet. Each individual was hit at least once, and most of them were hit many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they had run the gauntlet, or went through the gauntlet, what happened to those prisoners? Where did they go? Please don't look at the diagram. Just tell the Court what it is that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we switch the diagram off, please, and put it into evidence? I make an application for this diagram to become evidence as an exhibit in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The diagram you tender will be received, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this diagram will be received as Exhibit 144.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I've asked you what happened after the prisoners went through the gauntlet. Can you tell the Court, please, where they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As each one approached the end of the gauntlet, the soldiers were sending them to the right and lining them along the wall of the hangar, one by one along the wall, facing the wall, hands above their heads facing the wall. To the right, then to the right, and then again to the right. I'm sorry. To the right and then to the left, and then to the left. Once to the right and twice to the left. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember where you were located when you went into the actual hangar itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reached the far end of these markings, the opposite side facing the entrance. I was followed by a number of soldiers that have not been marked here. Prisoners. I meant prisoners, not soldiers. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people were actually inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the people from the five buses that arrived from the Vukovar Hospital and from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went into the hangar area, did you see what was happening inside the hangar initially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see. This was not in my view. It was around the door and then to the right and then along the wall. I wasn't actually able to see what was going on inside the hangar until I entered myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you entered, what did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once inside, I saw the prisoners, how they were lined up against the hangar wall, to the right, then to the left, and then to the left again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what way were the prisoners facing? In towards the centre of the hangar or towards the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As they were coming in and as they were being lined up, everyone was made to face the wall, hands above their heads facing the wall. Hands on the wall, facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did everyone do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe that was a part of their strategy on the part of those who had arrested us. As long as you keep a person with their hands in the air above their heads, that person poses no danger to anyone passing them, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any persons with uniforms inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I reached the end of the gauntlet, I came across an officer who grabbed me by the shoulder, pushed me and told me to get into the hangar, meaning for me to go in and look for a place where I could join the line of prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must ask the witness if you would please move your chair a little closer to the table and to the microphone. The interpreters are having difficulty catching all that you are saying. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again. Sorry, I see Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I appreciate very much my colleague interrupting this. I just have something to say about the transcript. What has not been recorded is the actual words that the officer told the witness. He said, "Go there," and this has not been recorded. This is page 31, lines 23 through 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps my colleague could re-ask the question, just in order to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again. Did you see any persons with uniforms inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, please, what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I reached the entrance, I came across a JNA officer who grabbed me by the shoulder and pushed me inside the hangar, telling me to go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I took this to mean was for me to go and join the line of prisoners inside, to find a spot, to join the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go there as he had indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But according to some rule or other written by I don't know whom, you would go to the right from the entrance and then to the left and again to the left, the prisoners lining up. That seemed too far away for me to walk, so I wanted to cut across the hangar and head straight for that free spot over there, in this line of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you did that, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not counting on the possibility of trouble, there were two soldiers standing at the entrance to the hangar, the two paramilitaries. One of them kicked me in my knee, my right knee, and the other hit me on my cheek just near the mouth with a crutch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eventually get to the wall and put your hands up as directed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After this incident, I caught the right moment, as it were, to run across, go all the way to the wall and take my place there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so what happened after that, then, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I forgot to say something. When this area was full of prisoners, the area in which I was, at the other end of the hangar there was a stack of hay, and all those who came after me were sent there, and those who were standing on that hay were watching the middle of the hangar, watching the prisoners, unlike those of us who had arrived earlier who had been forced to fix our eyes on the wall, to face the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to assess how long it took to disembark all the prisoners from the buses and bring them into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on what I could figure out and based on what I remember, the entire operation from the time we got off the buses until the time the last prisoner entered the hangar took about one hour. It was at about 1600 hours that everyone had been led into the hangar and inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to deal with timing in a slightly different way. If we use light, afternoon, early evening, and night-time, when you went from the house into the hangar, can you remember what the lighting was like at that time? The natural lighting, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll put it this way: Was the day bright, was it overcast, was it sort of semi-overcast? This is not something I could remember, but visibility was still very good, both inside the hangar and particularly outside in the open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the buses had completely disembarked all the passengers, how many team approximately were in that hangar? Was it in tens or hundreds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hundreds. Based on information obtained later on, 200 prisoners, civilians, wounded, and medical staff from the Vukovar Hospital were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was guarding the people inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were being guarded by regular JNA soldiers, the young ones, those who had escorted us on the buses. My impression was there were more of them there than on the buses. If there had been two on each bus, there must have been more there because the -- they totaled more than ten soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any dealings with any soldiers while you were against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These young soldiers were walking behind our backs, across the hangar, so a group of three young soldiers came up. One of them placed his automatic rifle on my back, saying, "If you have any money on you and if you don't give it to me, I'll kill you." He also said, "Somebody else is likely to take it from you anyway. You won't be needing it any longer. You are surrounded by cold-blooded murderers and you will all be killed tonight." I had my entire monthly salary in my pocket in an envelope. I put my hand inside my pocket. I pulled out the envelope and gave it to the soldier who had his rifle against my back. After I had given this to them, they moved away and did not touch me again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about being against the wall. Did you know the persons who were either side of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew one young man. I knew his parents' last name. Not him personally, probably not. He was aged about 17, and his name was Tomislav Baumgertner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was happening to Tomislav Baumgertner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked very young and rather small, puny. So these young soldiers started abusing him verbally, taunting him, asking if he'd been to front, if he'd served in the army, if he'd done anything against anyone else, something along these things, if he'd killed any of the soldiers of the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said he had done nothing, that he was only 17 years old - he said this a couple of times, actually - that he had been with his mother in the hospital. His mother worked in the hospital, she was a nurse, and this was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Tomislav Baumgertner indicate whether he knew any other persons in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Tomas Baumgertner? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. He was standing right next to me. We were in the same position. Whether those soldiers were satisfied with his answer or not, I don't know, but then he was asked whether he knew Dr. Mladen Ivankovic's sons. He answered that he knew the youngest son very well because they were schoolmates. Then the soldiers took him away from that group of people facing the wall, and I have no idea where they took him to. I was not able to see that. However, on my way out of the hangar, I saw him sitting on the ground in a separate group comprising about 10 or 12 victims or prisoners on the left side of the wall on the way into the hangar. They were all seated there, their backs to the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to return, please, to a clean copy of diagram 20193, please, the same diagram showing the warehouse, as it's described. Can that be shown, please? This is the diagram that you've seen before. Can I ask you, please, to look at the diagram. And I'm going to hold up to assist the Court and the witness to point out various parts of the diagram that I want him to direct his attention to. The first part of the diagram that I'd like the witness to observe, may I point to it, please, which is at the bottom of the diagram. Can the witness, look, please, where I'm pointing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the hay, the two circles or dots, whatever you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to deal with the two dots at the moment. You've referred to the hay. Can you show us where the hay is on your diagram, please? Just put a circle around it, a big circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were any of the prisoners located on the hay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why were they there; do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the way we were lined up, there was no free room there anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the two dots in front of the hay. Can you see them all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we -- before we deal with those dots, can you mark with an X, please, where you were standing against the wall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you were standing against the wall you've put an X. Can you put S there, please, the letter S. Now, can we deal with the two dots, please. I'm going to subdivide them into A and B. The dot that was nearest to you, what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dot that is nearest to me represents a prisoner, represents the exact spot where a prisoner was standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of that prisoner, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of that prisoner standing nearest to me at this dot, his name was Kemal Saiti.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, what was happening to Kemal Saiti inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following was happening to him: By this time, the paramilitary units had already begun to enter the hangar. They walked up to this hay and attacked this prisoner Kemal. I'm not sure what they were telling him. At any rate, they started to beat him. There were three, maybe four of them. He fell down on the concrete floor. They kicked him, jumped all over his stomach. Due to all the pain he probably turn around, so they jumped all over his back, kicked him until one of them grabbed him by the hair and banged his head several times against the concrete floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did this to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people who were very much like the people who had made up the gauntlet outside. Not regular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone attempt to stop the attack on Kemal Saiti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that I was able to see or hear, no one attempted to stop the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you -- would you be kind enough, please, to put a K, the letter K, beside the dot that represents the attack on Kemal Saiti.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can we deal with the second dot that is marked on this diagram. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second dot on this diagram represents the spot where another prisoner was standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that prisoner, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other prisoner was standing some distance from me, and I wasn't able to see anything. I only heard that some sort of a beating was taking place, and I think he suffered the same fate as the previous prisoner. However, on the hay itself, those prisoners who were watching the middle of the hangar, they were standing at a distance of perhaps one or two metres, they were watching, they told me the other prisoner was Damjan Samardzic and that he had suffered the same fate as Kemal before him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're aware, either from your direct knowledge or knowledge from others given to you, was there any attempt to stop the beating of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain standing against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stood against the wall for about 45 minutes facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did your position change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same soldiers who monitored us ordered us to turn around, face the middle of the hangar, sit on the floor, and lean with our backs against the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything occur to you while you were sitting in this position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I sat there, I don't know how long after we'd been ordered to sit down, the paramilitaries started walking in front of us. A group of about three or four of them stopped in front of me. They asked me how many of their soldiers I'd killed. I told them I hadn't killed anyone. I said that the last time I had occasion to shoot was when I did my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said that to them, did they reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of them -- and they were always in a group, they never went around individually. I guess one was always a leader and others were followers. So one of them offered me his rifle, I guess intending for me to show him whether I knew how to shoot or not. However, I didn't accept that, because I realised that ones who were with him were ready to turn their guns against me, if needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what then happened, then, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, some commotion arose so that both the soldiers and the paramilitaries started saying to each other, "Officers." I guess that indicated that their job was over. And automatically they stepped aside and dispersed within the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Before we proceed with the next piece of evidence, could I ask, please, for this marked diagram to be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this exhibit will be assigned the reference 145.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I wonder, please, if that could be removed now from the screen of the witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us about the word "officers," suggesting that officers were arriving. Did you see any officers arrive at the Ovcara building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't able to see that because the people provoking me or taunting me stood in front of me. Once they stepped aside and went elsewhere, I don't know where, I didn't see any officers then either entering or leaving the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time when you were in the hangar come face-to-face or see a person that you believed to be an officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except for this. Once I left the hangar, if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately I can't give evidence. Can I just deal, please, with inside the hangar, first of all, and then we'll deal with outside the hangar. But how was it that you came then to leave the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you kindly for the warning. Once these soldiers taunting me stepped aside, moved away from me, then an acquaintance of mine came by. We used to live in the same neighbourhood before. He knew me very well. He was a good friend of my son's. When he saw me there, he asked me what I was doing there. I explained the situation to him, told him I was arrested at the hospital and then brought there. He told me to come with him. I followed him across the hangar. We came to the entrance. This is where we came across an officer to whom he attempted to explain who I was, saying that he knew me and saying that he believed me to be innocent. The officer told him, "Take this man outside." However, he kept talking to him. I don't know what he was saying to him, because I stood a bit further away. Then the officer sort of gently pushed me out. My acquaintance was there, and together we went out of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to go into closed session, if I may, in relation to names to be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've been telling us about various matters, and you're about to tell us about your trip back to Vukovar. But looking back at your evidence, can you remember if you were able to recognise anyone at Ovcara whom you had seen at the JNA barracks that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for Milos Bulic. I saw him both in the barracks and in Ovcara. I didn't know the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just in very general terms tell us how you know this man called Milan Bulic? Where does he come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, not Milos but Milan. I have always known him as Milan, although some people called him Milos, but he corrected that. I know him because he was a butcher, and he used to work in the Vukovar Hospital, in the kitchens there as a butcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know to which unit he was attached while at the JNA barracks/Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, because I was not privy to such information. As I've told you, in the barracks he was in the group of the soldiers who behaved themselves more decently, the older ones who seemed to be either TO members or the JNA reserve soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to move on to the trip back to Vukovar and then deal with really not a large part of evidence. I would anticipate probably no more than about 20 minutes. I know it's a little early, but I also know that the witness has certain difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at half past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we deal then, please, with your trip to Vukovar? How many people were in the vehicle that went back towards Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could OTP turn off the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were seven of us who were returned to Vukovar, seven prisoners, two soldiers escorting us in the cab. One soldier and Mr. Cakalic were with the driver on the front seat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers themselves, are you able to say again to which unit they belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-031 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was quite dark, and it was difficult to see anything inside the jeep where we were. It was impossible to see anything at all.
